title: Ripple scenario
description: The question. Built by the UI controls or by the agent tool build_scenario(); validated with zod in the browser and with pydantic in the API. Fields that do not apply to the chosen type are ignored.

type.description: promo = discount for some weeks; price = permanent price change; new_city = launch in a city with no history.

label.description: Optional human title, e.g. '20% student coupon in Boston'.

cities.description: Training city names the change applies to. Empty or omitted = all training cities. Ignored when type is new_city.

segments.description: Segment names the change applies to. Empty or omitted = all segments. Cells outside the selection stay at baseline.

discount.description: promo only: fraction off, e.g. 0.2 for 20% off. net_price = base_price * (1 - discount).

weeks.description: promo only: how many weeks the discount runs, starting at week 1 of the horizon.

price_change.description: price only: fraction change for the whole horizon, e.g. 0.08 for +8%.

feature.description: Turn the feature flag on for the selected cells over the horizon.

candidate.description: new_city only: a name from posterior.candidates. Takes precedence over traits.

traits.description: new_city only: raw trait values in posterior.meta.trait_names order, used when candidate is not given.

new_city_shares.description: new_city only: expected segment mix. Defaults to the candidate's shares, else the training average.

new_city_price.description: new_city only: launch price. Defaults to base_price.

market_size.description: new_city only: multiplier on expected volume when the new city's addressable base differs from the training average. Defaults to 1.

unit_cost.description: Variable cost per unit. Defaults to posterior.meta.unit_cost.

fixed_cost.description: One-off cost of the change over the whole horizon (campaign spend, launch cost). Defaults to 0.

horizon.description: Weeks simulated, for both baseline and scenario.

seed.description: Seed for the new-city z draws, so the same scenario always gives the same numbers. Defaults to 7.
